newsitem.title: USA: Armstrong begins tender offer for Domco.
newsitem.headline: Armstrong begins tender offer for Domco.

text.p: Armstrong World Industries Inc. said Monday it has launched an all-cash C$488 million ($352 million) hostile takeover offer for Domco Inc.

Armstrong announced the bid a week ago and is suing Sommer Allibert SA, the Canadian company's controlling French shareholder, to prevent Sommer from merging its floor covering business, which includes Domco, with Tarkett AG, a competitor.
Armstrong, as a minority shareholder of Domco, also alleges that Domco directors have subordinated the company's and minority shareholders' interests to those of Sommer.
Armstrong, a global manufacturer and marketer of interior furnishings and ceiling systems as well as floor coverings, had sales of $2.16 billion in 1996.
The offer includes an all-cash purchase price of C$23.00 ($16.62) per common share, C$12.00 ($8.67) per warrant, and C$2,090.91 ($1,510.55) per C$1,000 ($722.44) principal amount of debentures.
Holders of warrants and debentures will be paid additional amounts to compensate for the early termination of their investment, Armstrong said.
Holders of warrants and debentures are not required to exercise or convert such securities to accept the offer, the company said.
Lancaster, Pa.-based Armstrong' stock rose $1.125 to $71.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in consolidated late trading.
